method: Actual in-app browser screenshots and native SVG DOM measurements; overview comparisons are fit previews and do not prove native-size legibility.

observations.finding: FrontierMosaic default closes its proved helper without opening adjacent computations. The shared-result trial is rejected for disproportionate area, despite expression gain.
The same relationship on unfamiliar BranchedMosaic is accepted: producer and consumers are shown, with a larger footprint. Decision is from measured layout, not family name.
Real editor default has 10 node elements; toggling adaptive detail and reopening the saved document yields 14 and matches command-line exports.
Default whole graph becomes shorter, with the same broad two-region organization. It remains sparse in places and dense around cross-links; fit-preview text is small.
One dependency-tree summary opens to the original token input, square-root computation, embedding, multiply and return. This demonstrates local reversibility, not complete large-graph UI performance.
Dedicated reference has stronger color, stage boundaries and compact aligned columns. Current generic graph has longer routes and more whitespace; overall reference convergence is not achieved.
The larger role trial is visibly much taller and more scattered. Rejection preserves default state; accepted arithmetic detail also has a measurable height cost.
Actual print SVG shows the shared result and paths into linear and addition operations. Native viewport shows part of the taller panel; XML and DOM measurement cover the full document.

remaining: Summary-level expression goals and global joint summary/detail selection
General DAG summaries and complete graph-set planning
Thousands-node simultaneous routing and interaction performance
